Goworowo Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Wólka Brzezińska, Poland

Demolished. Jews are first recorded in Goworowo in the 18th century; by 1921, 1,085 (91.4%) of 1,187 total residents were forced to leave the village entirely by German order in mid-September 1939. This cemetery is referenced in Goworowo parish visitation records from 1781, and again in an 1851 government letter; a stone wall enclosed the site by the interwar period, with a funeral house or caretaker's residence at the entrance. German forces used some matzevot for road and presbytery driveway reinforcement during WWII; postwar theft continued, eventually removing almost all tombstones and demolishing the wall and buildings. A drainage ditch and meadow use followed. In 1987, single tombstones were rediscovered on the land; in 1988, matzevot recovered from a nearby presbytery courtyard were relocated to the local library before eventual storage at the Commune Office warehouse.
